html:
The individual stories above (DA = RPEs, NE = unexpected uncertainty/adaptive gain, ACh = expected uncertainty/encoding mode, 5-HT = long-horizon value & cost, OXT/AVP = social precision & homeostatic coupling) are only locally true. In vivo, these systems talk constantly-through direct synapses, reciprocal hypothalamic/brainstem loops, heteroreceptor complexes, shared second-messenger pathways, and common targets (PFC, striatum, hippocampus, amygdala). The result is not six independent "knobs," but a low-dimensional control manifold that continuously retunes a high-dimensional world-model. A useful way to see this manifold is to map each transmitter to a small set of algorithmic hyperparameters and then watch how they co-regulate them as contexts, internal states, and horizons change.

In reinforcement-learning terms, dopamine mostly carries and gates error terms (derivatives of value and action expectations), serotonin biases the discount factor / planning depth and opportunity-cost accounting, noradrenaline sets learning rates and policy temperature in proportion to unexpected uncertainty, acetylcholine sets Kalman-like gains under expected uncertainty and flips the cortex between encoding and retrieval regimes, and oxytocin/vasopressin apply precision weighting to the "social slice" of the generative model, while coupling these computations to bodily budgets and life-history phase.

Multiple recurrent motifs make these systems interdependent:

First, descending cortical control: medial and orbital PFC, ACC, and insula project densely to VTA/SNc, LC, DRN/MRN, and basal forebrain, allowing high-level beliefs about task demands, costs, social context, and model adequacy to bias the entire neuromodulatory panel. A review maps the monoamine nuclei that project to prefrontal cortex (Figure).

Second, brainstem/hypothalamic hubs (PVN, LH, PAG, BNST, habenula/RMTg) integrate interoception, stress hormones, circadian signals, and nociception, and then co-drive LC, raphe, and VTA-explaining why energetic scarcity, inflammation, or chronic stress simultaneously steepen discounting (reduced 5-HT function), raise opportunity-cost signaling (increased tonic NE), and flatten dopaminergic exploration bursts. A 2026 review diagrams interacting brainstem and cortical modulatory pathways (Figure) 4.

Third, striatal convergence: cholinergic interneurons, comprising only  1-2% of striatal neurons, exert outsized influence by directly shaping dopamine release dynamics. When these giant aspiny interneurons pause their tonic firing ( 5-10 Hz), the resulting dip in nicotinic receptor activation on dopaminergic terminals creates a brief window of enhanced dopamine release probability. This pause-triggered dopamine surge can occur even without changes in VTA/SNc firing, effectively allowing the striatum to locally compute its own teaching signals 1. The temporal precision is remarkable: cholinergic pauses lasting 50-200ms can triple dopamine release within specific striatal compartments while leaving neighboring regions unaffected. This cholinergic gating becomes even more sophisticated through muscarinic signaling. M4 receptors on spiny projection neurons suppress cAMP when acetylcholine is high, effectively raising the threshold for dopamine-dependent plasticity. When cholinergic interneurons pause, this brake releases just as dopamine surges, creating a narrow temporal window where learning is maximally enabled-a molecular implementation of an AND gate for credit assignment. A 2026 review illustrates local dopamine–acetylcholine interactions (Figure) 5.

Push-pull dynamics in PFC

In prefrontal cortex, dopamine and norepinephrine implement complementary control over working memory dynamics despite both originating from catecholaminergic precursors 2. The inverted-U relationships governing their effects operate at different set points: optimal dopamine levels for working memory stability occur at moderate D1 receptor occupancy, while norepinephrine’s sweet spot for sustained attention requires lower tonic levels with preserved phasic responsiveness. Human resting-state imaging maps functional connectivity of dopamine-associated nuclei (Figure) 6. The same analysis maps connectivity of the locus coeruleus (Figure).

Crucially, these systems cross-regulate each other’s effects. High tonic norepinephrine (via α\alpha2A receptors) can functionally oppose D1 signaling by strengthening HCN channel conductances, effectively raising the bar for dopamine to stabilize persistent activity. This creates a push-pull dynamic where stress-induced norepinephrine release not only signals model uncertainty but actively destabilizes working memory representations-adaptively favoring cognitive flexibility when current strategies fail 3.

Temporal hierarchies and dependencies

Interactions are stratified by kinetics. Fast, phasic NE (tens to hundreds of ms) can momentarily override cortical attractors ("network reset"), after which sub-second ACh transients sharpen sensory gain to re-sample the world with high fidelity. Phasic DA (100-300 ms) then labels the surprising sample with an error signal for synaptic credit assignment. Over seconds to minutes, tonic DA biases vigor/exploitation, tonic NE sets the organism’s learning rate and exploration drive, tonic 5-HT integrates value and cost to determine patience and quitting thresholds, and minutes-to-hours OXT/AVP fields weight social cues and link policy to bodily budgets.

The LC-NE system acts as a critical state switch in this hierarchy. When tonic norepinephrine rises (signaling persistent model failure), it not only increases cortical gain but also modulates both dopaminergic and serotonergic signaling. High NE suppresses dopamine neuron firing via α\alpha2 receptors while simultaneously truncating serotonin’s temporal integration window-effectively telling the brain to abandon long-term plans and focus on immediate model revision. This creates a natural progression from patient, model-based planning (high 5-HT, low NE) through focused execution (balanced DA/ACh, moderate NE) to exploration and model updating (high NE, suppressed 5-HT).

The whole stack sits on even slower steroid and peptide backgrounds (glucocorticoids, leptin/ghrelin, cytokines) that reshape receptor densities, intracellular cascades, and even cell-type abundance-slowly moving the operating point of the control manifold.

In engineering terms, the brain implements a hierarchical PID/meta-controller: DA supplies largely derivative-like (error/change) terms, 5-HT contributes an integral-like persistence/value term, NE adjusts the adaptive gain and step size, ACh tunes the Kalman gain / observation model, and OXT/AVP reweight a socially restricted precision channel.

Convergent Modulation of Shared Effectors

Multiple neuromodulators often converge on the same molecular targets, creating rich combinatorial effects. Both dopamine (via D1) and norepinephrine (via β\beta receptors) activate PKA signaling, but with different spatial patterns and temporal dynamics. In hippocampal CA1, the coincidence of dopaminergic novelty signals and noradrenergic arousal signals synergistically enhances LTP through PKA, but only when acetylcholine is low (permitting strong Schaffer collateral transmission). This three-way interaction ensures that memories are preferentially strengthened when they are both novel (DA), behaviorally significant (NE), and arriving via external input rather than internal retrieval (low ACh). The review also summarizes convergence in intracellular signaling (Figure).

Precision, uncertainty, and arbitration

Framed in predictive processing/active inference, the core computation these systems share is precision control-i.e., setting the gain on different prediction errors and priors. NE inflates precision on sensory PEs when the model fails unexpectedly; ACh inflates precision on sensory channels when high noise is expected (encoding mode) and deflates top-down predictions; DA sets precision on value/state-transition PEs; 5-HT calibrates the precision of long-horizon value estimates vs. opportunity costs; OXT/AVP set precision on social prediction errors and on the interoceptive priors that couple social policies to bodily budgets.

Arbitration between model-free vs. model-based control, or between exploitation vs. exploration, is therefore naturally a chemically implemented precision game: high tonic NE + low 5-HT shortens horizons and heats policies; high 5-HT + moderate DA + low NE cools policies and deepens planning; high ACh with low DA locks the system into externally driven encoding; high OXT/AVP with DA/OFC engagement increases the precision of conspecific-related latent states, biasing credit assignment toward social cues.

To summarize, the neuromodulators do not form six orthogonal axes but a coordinated, partially redundant, partially specialized control sheet that lies on top of cortex-basal ganglia-hippocampus loops. It allocates precision, time, energy, and social weight; it partitions surprise into kinds (expected vs. unexpected, appetitive vs. aversive, private vs. social); and it ensures that a tiny number of slow, low-bandwidth channels can steer a vast, fast, content-rich world model without ever needing to encode that content themselves

Example Behavioral States and Their Neuromodulatory Signatures

Treat the following "neuromodulatory cocktails" as coarse heuristics, not laws.

Active Exploration/Foraging

High tonic NE: Elevated LC firing increases arousal and sampling behavior

Low-moderate tonic DA: Permits exploration rather than exploitation

High phasic DA: Responds to novel stimuli and unexpected rewards

Low 5-HT: Reduces behavioral inhibition and patience

Moderate ACh: Balances external attention with memory retrieval

Focused Task Learning

Moderate tonic DA: Maintains motivation without compulsive focus

High phasic DA: Strong RPE signaling for learning

Low-moderate tonic NE: Optimal for working memory stability

High phasic ACh: Enhanced sensory processing during cue presentation

Moderate 5-HT: Balances immediate rewards with future costs

Acute Stress/Threat Response

Very high phasic NE: Massive LC activation, network reset

Suppressed DA: Reduced reward seeking

Low 5-HT: Shortened temporal horizons

High ACh: Enhanced sensory vigilance

Elevated AVP: Defensive aggression, territoriality

Suppressed OXT: Reduced social approach

Focused exploitation/Consummatory Behavior

High tonic DA: Sustained motivation and vigor; sits near the D1 "inverted-U" optimum in PFC to stabilize task rules

Low tonic / high phasic NE: boosting moment-to-moment gain without globally heating policy temperature

High 5-HT: Behavioral persistence

Moderate ACh: supporting selective attention without fully flipping cortex into an encoding-dominant regime

Context-dependent OXT: Elevated during social feeding

Chronic Stress/Learned Helplessness

Chronically elevated tonic NE: Persistent hypervigilance

Blunted DA responses: Anhedonia, reduced RPEs

Depleted 5-HT: Loss of behavioral inhibition

Dysregulated ACh: Impaired attention switching

Altered OXT/AVP: Often reduced OXT, elevated AVP
